title: OLM: past, current and future
speaker: OLM A — context / host; name to confirm
bullets: Past: OLMv0, flawed namespace-local CRD visibility assumptions, SQLite, FBC
caption: Planned: helm+v2 and v2 schemas. Future: OCI catalog storage.
notes: Enumerate the timeline: past work includes OLMv0, SQLite catalogs and established file-based catalogs (FBC). Summarize OLMv0's flawed assumptions about namespace-local CRD visibility, independently managed APIs and watch-aware dependencies. CRD definitions are cluster-scoped shared APIs; custom resource instances may be namespaced, and controller watch scope is configured separately. Shared CRDs can couple operator upgrades. The flawed assumptions belonged to OLMv0's lifecycle model; Kubernetes' cluster-scoped CRD design is the underlying API boundary. Keep the OperatorGroup recap brief and explain how these lessons informed OLMv1. Current OLMv1 capabilities include ClusterExtension, version pins and webhooks. Ongoing development includes resource rollouts, user configuration, direct bundle installation and migration. Direct installation remains an open proposal in PR #2907 at the supplied 2026-10-09 check. Planned work includes Helm content using helm+v2 and v2 catalog schemas. OCI-native catalog storage and transport remain future work. Release-specific availability and feature gates require the source-version qualifications on the detailed slides. The 2025 deck already listed delivered features. A hands off to B after this overview at 04:00. Sources: ../kubecon-2025-slide-context.md slide 9; ../kubecon-2026-resource-assessment.md K-1/K-2/V0-2/V0-3; supplied feature-planning context.

title: User control of extension deployments
speaker: OLM B — lifecycle primitives; name to confirm
status: IN ACTIVE DEVELOPMENT / CONTROLLED BY FEATURE-GATE
caption: OLM applies user choices through operator configuration.
notes: Describe the deployment as a configuration exchange between users and the operator team. Users express environment, resource, placement, volume and metadata requirements through the package's configuration interface. Operator authors define schema and validation behavior. OLM carries the selected configuration into the deployment. DeploymentConfig is in active development and controlled by feature-gate; values are expressed through ClusterExtension configuration. Explain field-specific merge, replace and append behavior and annotation precedence. Validate example input and inspect the resulting deployment against the pinned source version. Watch-namespace pass-through leaves CRDs shared and supplies no watch-aware dependency management. caption: Structured output supports automation and models.
notes: Prepare OLMv1 ClusterCatalogs from the existing OLMv0 CatalogSources first. Then evaluate each operator installation for eligibility and preview its migration before transferring management. The check and preview actions evaluate operators; catalog preparation is the earlier prerequisite. The migration specification describes check, convert, rollback and cleanup with ClusterObjectSets. Functionality is supplied as library-olm. The example binaries illustrate library use. The user confirms structured output that supports automated processing, including models; it has not been independently exercised in this editing task. Eligibility checks have defined coverage. Retaining the namespace can reduce disruption; namespace changes may restart workloads or cause downtime. Validate recovery boundaries and source/gate versions for the selected case. This area is in active development. Sources: library-olm README/spec; ../kubecon-2026-resource-assessment.md; user migration guidance.

title: Planned Helm content support
speaker: OLM C — content/catalogs/contributions; name to confirm
lead: The rendering contract targets deterministic chart behavior.
bullets: Chart and values produce managed manifests
caption: Standard chart artifacts use a defined rendering contract.
notes: helm+v2 is the user-confirmed canonical discriminator for versioned OLM Helm packaging/catalog content. Standard chart OCI identity is used, with rendered manifests managed through OLM lifecycle behavior. User values are parsed and validated during rendering. Deterministic rendering is the design goal: features are allow-listed to exclude non-deterministic functionality, with compatibility fixtures required to validate the supported subset. Dependencies are vendored. Hooks and keep behavior are unsupported in the proposal. CRDs use templates/; crds/ is unsupported. Chart release-object mappings and restricted template functions require compatibility testing. Moving CRDs affects upgrade, deletion and data handling. Implementation of proposed gates remains independently unconfirmed. Native chart OCI identity and future OCI catalog storage are separate scopes. Sources: supplied Helm planning brief and feature-planning context.

title: Catalog performance and content types
speaker: OLM C — content/catalogs/contributions; name to confirm
lead: Design for lower catalog-processing cost and additional content types.
bullets: Direct version fields reduce property traversal
caption: File-based catalogs remain the established foundation.
notes: Credit established FBC capabilities: plaintext editing, composition, extensibility, package-level metadata and version/release properties already exist. The v2 work refines the representation and consumers: less duplicated CSV metadata, version/release fields available directly rather than via property traversal, and explicit mediaType dispatch for installable formats including Helm. Arbitrary FBC schema extensibility alone does not supply end-to-end installation support for a new content type. Catalog processing efficiency is a design benefit to validate, with no measured speedup claimed. Show the practical resolution/metadata work the new representation is intended to reduce. The user-confirmed near-term focus is flexible OLMv1 schemas; OCI-native catalog storage, transport and selective fetching are future work. Channels and legacy graphs are excluded from v2; lifecycle/constraint metadata remains open. Sources: https://olm.operatorframework.io/docs/reference/file-based-catalogs/ ; supplied v2 catalog brief; feature-planning context.
